### Study the dependence of the cumulative distribution differences by flux difference vs. $\alpha$.

<div style="margin-left: 10px"><a id="Figure_None"/><figure style="margin-left: 10px">   <img src="data:image/png;base64,"  > <br>  <figcaption>        
The overlayed cumulative distribution differences for the first and last bins of the BB,

between the first and last cells of the BB list.</div></figcaption></figure></div>

Conclude that the scaled cumulative distribution differences are consistent with the flux 
differences between the first and last cells of the BB list.

Check the ratio difference from one:

![output](data:image/png;base64,)

Difference from one: mean 5.9E-05, std 1.1E-13.<br> 
Do not understand why there do not seem to be fluctuations.

To generate a new cell with a given exposure fraction and alpha value, we need:
*  The cumulative distribution, $C(w,\alpha)$<br>
THis is derived from the full cumulative distribution $C(w,0)$, 
   and an analysis of the dependence on $\alpha$ derived from the first and last cells.

*  The number of weights $N$ to generate. <br>
For this we need $S$ for the cell, which is $S$ for the full cell 
times the exposure fraction. If we are simulating a given cell with a different $\alpha$, use its current value. <br> 
Then $ N = \frac{S}{\big< w/(1+\alpha w) \big>} $
where the angle brackets represent an average over $w$ sampled from $C(w,\alpha)$.


Use this normalized cumulative distribution difference to generate distributions 
for different values of $\alpha$.
